<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 45 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fcacbeda0f75e1dd4ccfc6073f7d6cd77e057ea4` — the merge of head `81e7c21ee054e53a435f069ffb44527e76336870` into base `020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fcacbeda0f75e1dd4ccfc6073f7d6cd77e057ea4 && git checkout fcacbeda0f75e1dd4ccfc6073f7d6cd77e057ea4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70 81e7c21ee054e53a435f069ffb44527e76336870 && git checkout -B drift-repro 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70 && git merge --no-ff 81e7c21ee054e53a435f069ffb44527e76336870

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dad002e6eca5aa4076e5b86825ec3bb727553270`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md + packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-field-meta.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner-reference-master-scope.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server-canonical-query-ast.test.ts, .changeset/33523-import-lookup-within-master.md, content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx; read only: packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts (step 2.9), ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx (dependentFilter), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, .github/workflows/ci.yml (the dogfood job and the Test Core plan)

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A3 · Fixes #33523 (p2) · narrowing face plus one skills rule. Read-only: the diff against its parent `4bba8b8f02`, the head tree, the card, and the check runs of this head and of `7b9cc0b17a` and `9467884463`, including the Check Changeset, Plan Test Core shards and two Test Core job logs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Where the scope comes from** (`referenceScopeSources`, import-coerce.ts). It applies only to a reference-type column with a `reference` and a resolver. Two sources:
  - The field's own `dependsOn`. Each entry whose sibling the row fills adds `{ param: sibling }`; `param` is the target field. That matches the picker: `LookupField`'s `dependentFilter` builds `f[param] = value` the same way.
  - Each `master_detail` field the target declares, when exactly one other single-value reference column of the row points at that master object and is filled. Zero such columns gives no scope. Two or more also give none, so bill-to and ship-to stay unscoped. A `dependsOn` entry on the same target field wins over the inferred master (`params.has(master.field)`).
  - A multi-value column never counts as a master. A blank cell or a `nullValues` token counts as not filled.
- **Order of resolution** (`coerceRow`). Unscoped columns resolve first. A scoped column resolves once all of its sources have settled, using their coerced ids. A source that failed, or that coerced to a non-scalar, adds nothing to the scope. If no pending column is ready, every pending column resolves unscoped (see N2). Errors are still reported in the row's column order, because the last loop walks `Object.keys(rawRow)`.
- **How the resolver applies it** (import-runner.ts). The scope is merged into every candidate's `where` (`{ [f]: display, ...(scope ?? {}) }`), so the `id` candidate is scoped too. A candidate field that the scope already fixes is skipped. The cache key carries the sorted scope, so a scoped answer never serves an unscoped question, or the reverse. A miss is still not cached.
- **Where the masters list comes from.** `mastersOf` reads the masters inside `servesReferenceTarget`, after the target's exposure is asked. A target the caller cannot serve gives `null`, and so no masters. It reads no record. The new `CALLERS` row in second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts classifies it.
- **RLS and FLS.** RLS is unchanged: it is the same `findData` with the same caller `context`, and the test "every lookup ... is read as the importing caller" asserts the context on every read. FLS is not quite unchanged (S1). The scope puts the target's master field, or a `dependsOn` `param`, into the caller's own `where`. plugin-security's predicate guard refuses a caller `where` on a field the caller cannot read (predicate-guard.ts; authz middleware step 2.9). The resolver's `catch` reads any throw as "field absent". So for such a caller every scoped candidate is refused, and the cell answers `reference_not_found`. This is fail-closed and discloses nothing. I found it by reading the code and did not run it.
- **Tests.** The new file has 10 cases. They cover all three acceptance criteria (both masters; a blank master is still ambiguous; not-found inside the master, including a pasted id from another master), column order, two master columns, `dependsOn`, a master cell that fails, and both match-key cases. The fake `findData` refuses `$` keys and operator values, so it cannot pass a query it does not implement. There is no real-engine or field-permission case. The PR body reports two ablations; I read them as the author's report and did not re-run them.
- **CI on this head**, read just before posting: see the CI line under ③. On `9467884463`, `Test Core` 4/8 and 5/8 were red on two `test:repo` tests. One was the core second-object-read pin (import-runner.ts was not classified). The other was the rest canonical-literal pin (the old `where` literal). `dad002e6ec` fixes both. On `7b9cc0b17a`, `TypeScript Type Check` was red; `9467884463` fixes it.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right: both the value and the arm.**
  - The value `yes` is earned. `packages/core/src/index.ts:117` re-exports `./utils/import-coerce.js` with `export *`. So `referenceScopeSources`, `ReferenceMaster`, `ReferenceScopeSource`, the optional `scope` / `sourceRow` / `referenceMasters` parameters, and `ExportFieldMeta.dependsOn` (re-exported at :116) all widen the root surface.
  - The arm is `(narrowing)`. A row that names master B and a detail only master A carries now answers `reference_not_found`, where it used to link A's detail. Under the closed pair the narrowing arm wins over the widening.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is right, so the level is `patch`.** No authorable key, value or default changes. `master_detail` and `dependsOn` mean what they meant; the import now honours them as one more door. The new refusal is judged against data (which master a detail row belongs to), the same line as the #33280 ruling (`none`, `patch`). Both entries are `patch`: `@objectstack/core: patch` and `@objectstack/skills: patch` (packages/skills exists).
- **The ADR-0087 disposition is right.** The changeset carries exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and both declaration lines. The narrowing arm (signal 4) is itself the breaking carrier. A `**BREAKING**` banner or `!` is optional (`breakingDeclaration`), and none was dropped. `no-migration-prescription` is open because the kind is not `narrowed`.
- **FROM/TO.** The `Clause-②` line spells both directions as before and after: `reference_ambiguous` becomes a resolved link, and a cross-master link becomes `reference_not_found`. "What stays" names the unchanged cases. AGENTS.md requires a FROM → TO mapping for a removed or renamed authorable thing, and nothing is removed here. What the changeset lacks is the one-line remedy for the narrowed row (S3).
- **The gate agrees.** Check Changeset passed on this head. Its log reads `.changeset/33523-import-lookup-within-master.md [clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)` and `✓ LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② yes (narrowing) and metadata-protocol none ... a non-protocol change at patch`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **(1) The dependents run.** I read this head's `Plan Test Core shards` log. All 8 shards start, and between them they name 61 of core's 62 direct dependents, counted from the head's package.json files. The 62nd, `@objectstack/dogfood`, is excluded from Test Core by design, and runs in the merge queue's `Dogfood Regression Gate` (see (2)). So CI covers the 57 the author left to it, and running 5 locally is acceptable once every Test Core shard on this head is green. The two `test:repo` reds on `9467884463` show the limit of the local run: it ran each package's `test` script, not `test:repo`, so the core and rest greens in the body did not include the two pins CI then turned red.
- **(2) The dogfood battery.** On a `pull_request` run the dogfood shards are skipped by design (`github.event_name != 'pull_request'`). They run on every merge-queue entry, and `Dogfood Regression Gate` is a required context, so the full battery runs before this lands. Three dogfood files drive the import on a real engine: `import-lands-readable-rows`, `import-reference-exposure` and `import-user-field-target`. A local hang after 1689 passing lines says nothing either way about this diff. It does not block. A targeted local run of those three files would be the proportionate reading to put in the body.
- **(3) The Verification section has to be refreshed before the PR leaves draft.** It names the heads `2c905cc01c` → `7b9cc0b17a`. It does not cover `9467884463` or `dad002e6ec`, or the two `test:repo` reds those commits fixed. It still says `service-automation` and `runtime` are NOT MEASURED, with their readings on the card instead. And the "Full dogfood" line points to a reading that did not complete. (S2)
- **CI:** 68 check runs on this head, read just before posting: 58 success, 10 skipped, none failed or pending. The successes include all 8 `Test Core` shards and the `Test Core` roll-up, all 16 `Test UI` shards, `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Lint · ESLint` and `Check Changeset`. The skipped runs include the dogfood shards and `Dogfood Verify CLI`, which do not run on a pull request. `mergeable_state: clean`.
- **Inferred masters go further than the picker.** `LookupField` narrows only by a declared `dependsOn` (and `lookupFilters`). The import also infers the master from `master_detail`, which #33523 asks for. So for a lookup with no `dependsOn`, the import is now stricter than the form. That is the declared narrowing; see N4 for the wording.
- **No cross-tenant path.** A scope only adds equalities to the caller's own read. The scope value is an id the caller's own lookup resolved, and the tenancy wall and RLS are still injected by the engine.
- **Draft.** The PR is a draft, authored by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. It touches `skills/**` (Tier H), so it lands by the maintainer's approval.
- N1 (nit): in the match-key pass, `scoped` is built only for the key cells. A source column outside them is coerced unscoped, even when the row's own pass would scope it (a chain such as account → contract → milestone). So the docblock's claim that a key is grouped "by the same id the row's own pass resolves" holds for one level of master, not for a chain.
- N2 (nit): when no pending column is ready, every pending column resolves unscoped. That includes a column whose only source sits behind a cycle without being part of it. The docblock says only "columns scoped by each other in a cycle". The fallback behaves as on `main`.
- N3 (nit): the scoped cache key and the unscoped key share one string space (`obj::display` against `obj::display::[...]`). A display value that itself ends in `::[["field","id"]]` can collide. That needs a record actually named that way, within one import and one caller.
- N4 (nit, prose): the docs and changeset say the scope works "as the record form's picker narrows its candidates". That holds for `dependsOn`. The `master_detail` inference has no counterpart in the picker.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Against #33523 and the spec on `main`.** The change does what the card asks: masters A and B each resolve their own detail, a row with no master keeps the object-wide lookup and its tie, and a name absent under the row's master answers `reference_not_found`. The tests pin all of these. The relationships.md note says the same in three lines and matches the code. The deleted cross-references and "✅ Correct" stubs only pointed to sections that are still there.
- **The narrowing.** It takes away no declared capability: no spec key or doc promised that a lookup cell resolves across masters. It makes the master relationship the record form already narrows by hold at the import door too. Two things go further than declared. Neither is a must-fix:
- **S1 (should-fix): the FLS face is undeclared, and the body's "RLS/FLS are unchanged" is not accurate.** Take a caller who cannot read the target's master field, or a `dependsOn` `param`. On `main`, that caller's row with a unique detail name resolved. Now it answers `reference_not_found`, a code that is wrong for a record the caller can read. Either change closes this:
  - (a) When every candidate of a scoped lookup threw, retry it unscoped. That gives the same answer as `main`, with no new disclosure.
  - (b) Name this case in the changeset's narrowing and in the docs.
  Either way, correct the body's FLS sentence.
- **S2 (should-fix, before ready-for-review): refresh the Verification section** for `dad002e6ec`. Name the two `test:repo` reds and their fix, add the `service-automation` and `runtime` readings, and say that the local package runs were `test` and did not include `test:repo`.
- **S3 (should-fix): give the narrowed row its remedy in the changeset.** A pasted id is scoped too, so a row that really means another master's detail has no way through in one import. The remedy is to correct the master cell, or, when the cross-master link is intended, leave the master column out of the import and set it in a second update.
- **Otherwise the design holds.** A scope is only extra equalities on the caller's own read. Ambiguous and zero masters fall back to the old lookup. A failed master cell scopes nothing and already fails the row. The match-key pass uses the same scope (save N1).

Implemented-by: `claude/area-A3-33523`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cxDxAYxdtDhtR1kQQe`

**VERDICT: PASS**
The declaration (`yes (narrowing)`, `none`, `patch`, one ADR-0087 marker) and the scoping hold at this head. S1 to S3 should be fixed before the PR leaves draft; S2 is a precondition for ready-for-review. N1 to N4 are nits. CI on this head is green. The full dogfood battery runs in the merge queue.

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `81e7c21ee054e53a435f069ffb44527e76336870`

Scope: skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md + packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-field-meta.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner-reference-master-scope.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server-canonical-query-ast.test.ts, .changeset/33523-import-lookup-within-master.md, content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx; read only: packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts (step 2.9), ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx (dependentFilter), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, .github/workflows/ci.yml (the dogfood job and the Test Core plan)

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A3 · Fixes #33523 (p2) · narrowing face plus one skills rule. Read-only: the diff against its parent `4bba8b8f02`, the head tree, the card, and the check runs of this head and of `7b9cc0b17a` and `9467884463`, including the Check Changeset, Plan Test Core shards and two Test Core job logs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Delta at `81e7c21ee0` (session_016WV4cztXwcRKcZdDqJmbSn).** The head is one commit on `dad002e6ec` with a single parent, so no merge of `main` is involved. `git diff dad002e6ec 81e7c21ee0` touches four files: the changeset, `import-mappings.mdx`, and docblocks in `import-coerce.ts` and `import-runner.ts`. Every changed `.ts` line is a `*` or `//` comment line (a filter for anything else finds none), so no code line changed. The judgments below about the code at `dad002e6ec` hold unchanged at this head.
- **Delta: the new FLS sentences match the code.** Changeset "Field permissions", the docs paragraph and the body's Resolver bullet all say a caller who cannot read the target's master field, or a `dependsOn` `param` field, gets `reference_not_found` for a scoped cell. I traced it at this head. `mastersOf` (import-runner.ts) reads the `master_detail` fields off the declaration and does not filter by field permission, so the scope is still built for such a caller. The resolver merges the scope into every candidate's `where`, `id` included, so every candidate carries the field. Step 2.9 of plugin-security's authz middleware runs `assertReadableQueryFields` against the caller's own read AST, before RLS injection, and throws `PermissionDeniedError` on a non-readable field. The resolver's `catch` skips the candidate, the match stays `{}`, and `coerceFieldValue` maps `match.id === undefined` to `reference_not_found` (import-coerce.ts). "It fails closed and discloses nothing" holds. "RLS is unchanged" holds: same `findData`, same caller context, and RLS is injected after the guard as before. Small imprecision, not an item: the guard also refuses a field the caller sees partly masked or that only an agent can read (`computeQueryGuardFieldPerms`). "Cannot read" covers the common case.
- **Delta: the items.** S1 is resolved by option (b): the narrowing in the changeset's `Clause-②` line and in the body, a "Field permissions" paragraph and a docs paragraph name the case, and the body now says RLS is unchanged and FLS is not. S2 is resolved: Verification is rewritten for `81e7c21ee0`. It names the `7b9cc0b17a` and `9467884463` reds and their fixes, and says the earlier local runs were `test`, not `test:repo`. It adds `test:repo` for core and rest, local runs of `service-automation` and `runtime` among the five dependents, and the three dogfood import files (17 passed). S3 is resolved: the remedy is in the changeset, the docs and the body, and covers the FLS case (grant read, or leave the master column out). N1 is fixed as prose in the `coerceRow` docblock, the runner comment, the changeset and the body ("one level of master"). N2 is fixed in the `coerceRow` docblock and the body ("a cycle, or a column whose source waits behind one"). N4 is fixed: the picker sentence now covers only `dependsOn`, and the `master_detail` inference is said to have no picker counterpart. N3 is carried in the body's Acceptance notes.
- **Delta: the declaration is unchanged.** The body and changeset still read `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`.
